A package is a documented bundle of functions, compiled code, and data.
Packages exist to make one specific job easy.

# Installing a Package

## From CRAN

Check the [full list of CRAN packages](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/available_packages_by_name.html).
If a package isn't already installed, install it with `install.packages()`.

```{r}
head(data.frame(installed.packages())[c(1, 3:5)], 5)
```

The installed-packages matrix has a `Package` column, easy to check with
`installed.packages()[, "Package"]`:
```{r}
all_packages <- installed.packages()[, "Package"]
"pacman" %in% all_packages
```

Install only if missing:
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
if (!"pacman" %in% all_packages) {
  install.packages("pacman", repos = "http://cran.us.r-project.org")
}
```

# Loading a Package

`library()` (from base R) makes a package's functions available:
```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(pacman)
```

`pacman::p_load()` loads a whole list of packages at once, installing any
that are missing:
```{r eval=FALSE}
pkg_list <- c("tidyverse", "ggplot2", "lubridate", "flextable")
p_load(pkg_list, character.only = TRUE)
```

## Package documentation

```{r eval=FALSE}
help(package = "pacman")
```
The full documentation is also available under RStudio's
**Files | Plots | Packages | Help** pane.

## Suppressing package startup noise

`tidyverse` (and others) print a message on load that you usually don't
want in a rendered report:
```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

# The `dplyr` Package

`dplyr` is part of `tidyverse` and provides a consistent grammar for data
manipulation, which reads especially well combined with the pipe (`%>%`,
covered in Chapter 12).

The most-used `dplyr` verbs are:

* `select()` — keep a subset of columns
```{r}
iris %>% select(1:4) %>% names()
iris %>% select(-Species) %>% names()
```

* `filter()` — keep a subset of rows matching a condition
```{r}
iris %>% filter(Species == "setosa", Petal.Length > 1.4) %>% head(3)
```

* `arrange()` — reorder rows
```{r}
iris %>% arrange(desc(Sepal.Length)) %>% head(3)
```

* `rename()` — rename columns
```{r}
iris %>% rename(PetalLength = Petal.Length) %>% names()
```

* `mutate()` — add or transform columns
```{r}
iris %>% mutate(Ratio = Petal.Length / Petal.Width) %>% head(3)
```

* `summarise()` — collapse a group into one row
```{r}
iris %>% group_by(Species) %>% summarise(mean = mean(Petal.Width), .groups = "drop")
```
